## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the staged sending down of the Quran and on the occasions of particular parts, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
- How the staged sending down fits with the sending down in a night or a month is a question of interpretation; the verses do not answer it. A scholar should decide whether the page says anything about it.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Sent down in stages  (`#sent-down-in-stages`)

Cited ayat: 17:106, 25:32

> **17:106** وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلًا

> **25:32** وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ وَرَتَّلْنَٰهُ تَرْتِيلًا

### Claims

**c1** (17:106): God says that He separated the Quran into parts so that the one addressed might recite it to the people over a period, and that He sent it down in stages.

**c2** (25:32): Those who disbelieved asked why the Quran was not sent down upon him all at once.

**c3** (25:32): The verse answers that it is so in order that God may make firm the heart of the one addressed with it, and says that God set it out in measured sequence.

### One-minute summary

God says that He separated the Quran into parts, so that it might be recited to the people over a period [c1]. Those who disbelieved asked why it was not sent down all at once [c2], and the answer given is that God makes firm the heart of the one addressed with it [c3].

### Complete story

God says that He separated the Quran into parts so that the one addressed might recite it to the people over a period, and that He sent it down in stages [c1].

Those who disbelieved asked why the Quran was not sent down upon him all at once [c2]. The verse answers that it is so in order that God may make firm the heart of the one addressed with it, and says that God set it out in measured sequence [c3].

### Deep study

The verses at 17:106 and 25:32 speak of the same manner of sending down [c1][c3]. The verse at 17:106 gives a purpose of the parts: recitation to the people over a period [c1]. The verse at 25:32 records an objection and gives a purpose of its own: making firm the heart [c2][c3]. The words for separating, for a period and for measured sequence are read in more than one way [c1][c3].

### Kids mode

God sent the Quran down in parts, not all at once [c1]. Some people who did not believe asked why it was not sent down all at once [c2]. The answer is that God makes the heart of the one who receives it firm with it [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the staged sending down as a kindness to the heart of the one who received it [c3]. Another is that it presents it as a help for reciting to the people over a period [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how many parts there were, how long the sending down lasted, or the intervals between the parts. The verses say only 'over a period' and 'in stages'.
- Not established: who the people were who asked why it was not sent down all at once, or when they asked.
- The Arabic verb in 17:106 can be read as 'separated' or as 'made distinct'; the draft keeps 'separated' and a scholar should decide.
- The Arabic word rendered 'set out in measured sequence' can also mean 'recited slowly'; this draft keeps the wider rendering.
- Not established: how this relates to the verses that speak of the Quran being sent down in a night or a month. The verses here do not mention a night.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the manner and order in which the parts came. None is used in the story texts.
